newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong to keep "free" local phone calls for now.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong to keep "free" local phone calls for now.

text.p: Hong Kong telephone users would continue to enjoy "free" local calls after most respondents in a recent survey opted to maintain the status quo, a senior telecommunications official said on Thursday.
"I...do not wish to recommend at this stage any particular option for changing the existing flat-rate pricing structure," said Alexander Arena, head of the Telecommunications Authority.
Most Hong Kong telephone users currently pay a flat monthly fee for a telephone line and local calls are not measured or charged for.
Arena said in a statement that more studies would be conducted on aspects such as traffic management, network costs to refine his proposals on pricing structure reform.

The statement came after a two-month survey by the Authority to study ways to keep up with expanding usage by a growing number of Internet and other non-voice telephone users putting pressure on existing local telephone lines.
Earlier this year, dominant local telephone service provider Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd said the territory was not ready to shift to a system of measured local calls.
